summary: Bound a resuming event stream's catch-up to 256 events / 1 MiB (else replay nothing and omit INFRA-492's X-Dispatch-Event-Replay: complete header so the client refetches once), dedupe the live loop on one cursor instead of the sentDuringCatchup map, encode each event once in the relay, make the relay the one event-log reader per process that also feeds the delivery hub, stop both at zero subscribers (generation objects), send comment mentions after the response through per-recipient FIFO lanes with a 10 s shutdown drain and a startup recovery pass, cap agent-stream viewers at 8 MiB of queued frames, move the stage3 production audits off full stream replay, and measure a restart with 50 streams on INFRA-589's harness before and after.

lanes.agreement: X-Dispatch-Event-Replay: complete only when INFRA-606's bounded replay was sent; whichever merges second applies it; no web change, no reset frame (told its architect over Envoy).

Head is the relay cursor read with the subscription under the relay mutex held across publish+advance; INFRA-591 replaces the relay's cursor and id>cursor reads with events.Horizon; hub has no read of its own (planner agreed over Envoy).
Restart scenario lands in INFRA-606's PR on packages/envoy/loadtest, building on legion/INFRA-589 until it merges; never patch the archive (planner's answer over Envoy).
Relay and hub reads go through store.Pool.Live(), the mention sender through store.Pool.Background(); whichever merges second moves the call sites.
Informed: no outbox edits; relay feed available for the outbox wake.

risks: INFRA-589's harness must exist (main or its branch) before T1 and T9; if it does not when T2-T8 are done, the implementer tells the architect at once, since the architect requires both numbers before testing.
Bringing main into the branch for INFRA-589's harness is a real need (the files exist nowhere else); the implementer states it when doing so.
Recovery runs in every Dispatch process at start; it sends only attempts no live sender holds, through the claim protocol.

findings.finding: INFRA-591 removes the commit-order lock that the int64 dedupe and the relay/hub id>cursor reads rely on; merge order and the meaning of head must be agreed.
findings.answer: Agreed with INFRA-591's planner: head is the relay's published cursor read with the subscription under the relay mutex held across publish+advance; INFRA-591 swaps the relay's cursor and read for events.Horizon; whichever merges second adapts (plan Lanes, T2, T3).

findings.finding: INFRA-492's replay header would claim completeness for a stream INFRA-606 chose not to replay, depending on merge order.
findings.answer: Rule told to INFRA-492's architect: complete only for a sent bounded replay; Go test asserts no complete header over the bound; no reset frame (plan Decision 2, T3).

findings.finding: Relay/hub stop-restart races: subscribe vs stop, old goroutines publishing after restart, WaitGroup Add vs Wait, flapping cost, hub state to recreate.
findings.answer: Generation objects with own context/stream/cursor; count and start/stop under one mutex; stopped generation publishes only to its own subscriber-less stream; Add under the mutex refused after lifetime ends; flapping cost arithmetic in Decision 4; hub generation owns ready/wakes/barrier/cursors/fresh state and goroutines check currency under h.mu (T2, T4).

findings.finding: Hub fed from the relay needs a cursor hand-off, overflow rule, reset rule, and has a payload cost; hub tests must be rewritten.
findings.answer: Hub trusts the relay's ordered feed and needs no cursor; 1024-slot buffer covers a relay page; feed close (overflow, reset, test hook) reloads p0 and dirties every view; payload cost stated; delivery_live_hub_test.go rewrite listed (T4, Tests).

findings.finding: Mention resolution stays in the request, so 'a slow listener does not delay the response' is ambiguous.
findings.answer: Plan keeps resolution (it fixes the event's suppression and pins) but makes it concurrent; sends, rechecks and settles leave the request; recorded as a spec departure for the architect (Decision 5, Departures).

findings.finding: 'In order' for mention delivery is ambiguous (per comment, per target, per session; cross-process).
findings.answer: Per recipient (pinned session id, else target) in the order this process accepted the comments; concurrent requests and two processes unordered, as today; tested with sequential comments (Decision 6).

findings.finding: Lifetime is cancelled at SIGTERM, so a lifetime-bound sender would cancel in-flight sends; drain position, queued items and queue bound unspecified.
findings.answer: Sender context WithoutCancel(lifetime) cancelled 10 s after lifetime ends, overlapping the HTTP/document drain inside stopGrace; no queued send started after SIGTERM; waitBackground waits; 4096-item bound with overflow left pending for recovery; shutdown_test.go covers it (Decision 7, T5).

findings.finding: The startup recovery pass has no source in the spec and risks a startup storm, stale sends, taking another replica's attempts, and a timer.
findings.answer: Kept because async sends queued at SIGTERM would otherwise strand (today the HTTP drain sends them): one pass at start, lanes bound concurrency, one-hour window, claim protocol prevents double sends, no timer; the claim-lapse re-check was dropped (Decision 8).

findings.finding: stage3 production audits replay the whole stream since a baseline and would break under the bound; listener tests and several docs also depend on current behaviour.
findings.answer: T7 moves the audits to the issues?updated_since method stage4b uses; cmd/listener tests added to the test command; doc list in T8.

findings.finding: N=256 and 1 MiB have no source; a refetch may cost more than a replay.
findings.answer: Derivation from the load reproduction's per-request and per-event costs in Decision 1; the harness counts the browser's refetch so the after-number cannot hide its cost; probe counts rows, not id differences; relay page size kept separate.

findings.finding: Measurement acceptance has no pass condition, and the harness cannot resume, restart mid-step, follow a new pid, make mentions reach Send, or model the refetch.
findings.answer: T1 adds resume, stale streams, refetch modelling, restart via stack.sh with stack.json PID re-read, session capabilities and an RTT proxy on Dispatch's ENVOY_URL; expected outcomes stated in the Acceptance table without thresholds to game.

findings.finding: A 2 MiB agent-stream budget can be stricter than today during the 2 s replay wait; the oversize-frame clause is unreachable.
findings.answer: Budget raised to 8 MiB sized from the 100 ms snapshot throttle and the 2 s replay wait; oversize clause dropped (NATS caps a frame at 1 MiB); test that a viewer survives the replay wait with 20 frames of 300 KiB (Decision 9, T6).

findings.finding: Encode-once must keep live and replayed frames byte-identical and shared frames immutable; Stream[T] edits INFRA-591's broker.go.
findings.answer: One encodeSSEFrame used by relay and catch-up; nothing mutates shared values; broker.go change limited to the type parameter, covered by the INFRA-591 agreement (T2).

findings.finding: Other lanes: INFRA-590 adding its own LISTEN, INFRA-592 pools and admission, INFRA-63 replicas, INFRA-594, INFRA-607, INFRA-596.
findings.answer: INFRA-590 told the relay feed exists and no outbox edits; INFRA-592's Live()/Background() pools adopted; one read per commit stated per process; INFRA-594/596/607 have no file overlap with this plan's edits.

specDepartures.spec: Mention delivery runs off the request path, in order, with a test that a slow listener does not delay the comment's response.
specDepartures.plan: The claim, recheck, send and settle of each mention leave the request. The one listener lookup per mention that pins its session and decides the route copy's suppression stays in the request, made concurrent, so a slow listener delays the response by one round trip rather than none. The slow-listener test slows the send and recheck; a second test shows k lookups cost one round trip.
specDepartures.evidence: comment_create.go:371-390 resolves mentions before the transaction and writes the result into the comment.created event (SuppressedAuthors, SuppressedRoute, each mention's session_id); moving it after commit changes what that event records and which route copy is suppressed.

acceptance: Mention delivery runs off the request path, in order, with a test that a slow listener does not delay the comment's response.
